Return `edits` (exact old text found once, and its replacement) using the anchors given; change nothing else. In docs/lanes.md, directly before the heading line "## The rented lane" (use that heading line as the anchor and keep it) add two sections. First "## Haiku rate limits and lane concurrency": Anthropic rate limits for claude-haiku-5-5 at our tier, read from the response headers of a 1-token call on 2026-10-16: 10,000 requests per minute, 10,000,000 input tokens per minute, 2,000,000 output tokens per minute (12,000,000 tokens per minute in all). Measured Haiku task profile (the 11-task comparison): about 9.6k input and 2.7k output tokens per task, about 11.8 s per task, so one agent sends about 5.1 requests per minute, 49k input tokens per minute and 13.6k output tokens per minute. Maximum agents by each limit: requests 1,960; input tokens 204; output tokens about 147 (the binding one), so about 147 Haiku agents at full speed and about 100 with a 70 percent margin. One more rule: Anthropic estimates output tokens per minute from each request's max_tokens when it starts and corrects it when it ends, so agents times requests per minute times max_tokens must stay under 2,000,000: at the default 8192 that is about 47 agents for fast 12 s tasks, at 4096 about 95, at 2048 about 190. The lane's default concurrency is 32 (safe at the default 8192 even for fast tasks, about 66 percent of the limit); raise it with lanes.anthropic.concurrency in the machine config up to about 96 only when jobs set maxOutputTokens of 4096 or less; 429 answers are already backed off and retried by the lane. Second "## Which lane gets a ticket": Router rule (owner decision): Haiku (anthropic) is the default worker lane; the rented GPU lane is used by automatic routing only when at least 700 non-sensitive tickets are ready in the run (the number of auto jobs in the manifest; RENTED_MIN_READY, overridable with lanes.rented.minReady) and the job carries its contract; Codex takes hard tickets (a job with hard: true goes to Codex first); sensitive jobs never go to the rented lane; one failure on the rented lane escalates to Haiku, then Codex.
